overview.title: Silhouette of a Protected Reserve
overview.p1: The Îles Purpuraires (Mogador) sit just offshore as Essaouira’s seaward emblem. They are an important bird reserve; landing is heavily regulated and often forbidden without authorisation.
overview.p2: Most visitors enjoy the silhouette from the Skala or the beach. Boat trips that approach without landing may be offered — always confirm what is legal that season.
overview.p3: Ancient purple-dye history adds depth if you read a short note before you go.

q1.question: Can I land on the islands?
q1.answer: Usually not without special permission. Confirm with authorities or licensed operators.

q2.question: Are boat trips worth it?
q2.answer: For sea time and views, yes — when weather and rules allow.

q3.question: Best viewpoint on land?
q3.answer: Skala de la Ville and parts of the beach and ramparts.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Mogador Islands?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and local context.

q5.question: Is Mogador Islands suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision near drops, wind or busy lanes.
